answer: A beacon-seeded time lock is one workable defence. Each epoch the network publishes a fresh random seed, and a new identity must run a sequential hash chain from it for ten minutes before it may attest once. The chain resists parallelisation, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand staggered waits. An honest agent pays that once at signup, then renews by staying present. Forging identity becomes a purchase of wall-clock time. A meadow of fresh addresses stops reading as a crowd: the graph thins into a sparse nebula, and each bridge between clusters is billed in seconds nobody can borrow.
